stem: Which statement best describes continuous quality improvement in healthcare?

options.A: End the improvement process once the organization proves that a minimum external standard has been met for the current review period.
options.B: Focus primarily on identifying the individual responsible after an adverse event instead of examining the processes that shaped performance.
options.C: Limit quality-improvement work to external accreditation surveys rather than integrating measurement and testing into routine operations.
options.D: Use an ongoing, systematic, data-driven process that sets goals, tests changes, measures performance, learns from results, and continues improving care processes.

rationale: AHRQ EvidenceNOW describes quality improvement as a systematic, data-driven process for managing change. It recommends setting improvement goals, identifying and testing changes, selecting measures, collecting and reviewing data regularly, comparing results with goals/benchmarks, and acting on the data. D best represents continuous quality improvement.
educational_objective: Describe continuous quality improvement as an ongoing systematic process of setting goals, testing changes, measuring results, learning, and refining care processes.

source_original.rationale: AHRQ describes quality improvement as a systematic, data-driven process in which teams identify priorities, test changes, measure performance and continue learning and improvement over time.

correction_summary: Retained the continuous-QI construct and key D, aligned the final wording to AHRQ's systematic data-driven process and explicit test/measure/act cycle, verified Management of Care p.7, and reduced difficulty from hard to medium.

audit_findings.exact_locator: EvidenceNOW Key Driver 2 data-driven QI process
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item accurately represents QI as systematic, iterative measurement/testing/action rather than one-time compliance or blame assignment.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because QI is ongoing rather than ending at minimum external compliance.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because QI examines processes/systems and improvement opportunities rather than focusing primarily on blame.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because QI is integrated into routine practice, not limited to surveys.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only D includes the systematic iterative data-driven elements of QI.
audit_findings.cueing: All options contrast different conceptual approaches to quality work; D is supported by source content.
audit_findings.blueprint: Management of Care — performance and quality improvement.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read AHRQ Key Driver 2, NCSBN Management p.7 screenshot, all options, rationale and objective. D remained uniquely correct.
